title: Draw a 40 mm circle with a school compass, its point kept in the centre mark, then lay the compass down
keywords: light grip on a small handle
instruction: Draw the circle around the centre mark on the pad with the compass standing there (it is already set to a 40 mm radius), then lay the compass down on the desk.
context: Drawing a circle with a pair of compasses is school geometry homework almost everyone has done. A person spins the knurled handle between finger and thumb; a two-finger gripper cannot roll it, so it must carry the 8 mm handle round a 20 mm circle about the steel point while turning with it, holding it lightly so the compass rocks in its fingers and both points stay on the paper. Pressing hard breaks the pencil's point or opens the friction hinge so the circle spirals (a how-to guide: "push the pencil into the paper ... widens the radius"); a sideways shove or a lift skids the point out of its mark. A wrist turns only about 240 degrees, so part-way round the hand must open, turn back and take the handle again while the 32 g compass balances on its two points.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) A4 writing pad, loose: 21.0 x 29.7 cm (long side along y), 6 mm thick (50 sheets of 80 g/m2 paper on a 1 mm card back), 0.30 kg; x 10.95 to 32.05, y -21.85 to 7.85. A pencilled cross marks the centre at x 21.5, y -10.0 (3 cm right of the pad's middle); the compass point has pricked it (a hole 1.0 mm across, 1.5 mm deep). (2) Metal school compass holding a pencil (like Helix G05048), loose, already set to a 40 mm radius: steel head 14 x 9 x 12 mm with a knurled handle 8 mm across and 22 mm long on top (top 12.4 cm above the desk); needle leg fixed to the head, ending in a 0.7 mm steel point; pencil leg on a friction hinge that holds until 0.10 N m acts on it (1.1 N at the pencil's point across the legs), clamping a sharpened 7 mm pencil stub; 92 mm from hinge to each point; 32 g in all. It stands on its two points: the steel point in the pricked mark, the pencil's point on the paper at x 25.5, y -10.0, the legs in the x-z plane. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step: where the steel point and the pencil's point are relative to the centre mark (in the pad's frame), the pencil's contact force on the pad, the compass's pose, and each finger's collision-hull points. The pencil draws while its point presses on the paper or is within 0.1 mm of it; the circle drawn is counted in 1-degree steps along the path of the pencil's point (each degree once, a dot where it stood not counted) wherever it draws at a radius within 1.5 mm of 40 mm. 0 for the rest of the run once a rule is broken: the steel point skidded (more than 1 mm from the mark while its tip is in the paper or less than 0.3 mm above it); the pencil pressed with more than 5 N (its point breaks); the pencil drew more than 3 mm off the 40 mm circle (a spiral or stray mark). Otherwise 0.8 x degrees drawn / 360. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): at least 355 deg drawn, the compass lying on its side (hinge axis within 30 deg of vertical, head within 3 cm of the desk), every finger point 2 cm or more from its handle and legs, and still (head under 1 mm in 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a transparent overlay with circles of radius 38.5 and 41.5 mm and a 3 mm band beyond, centred on the prick, gives the degrees of line inside the band; a second prick or a point scratch, a broken pencil point, or a line outside the band scores 0; lying and let go are checked on the video.
reset_notes: Tear off the drawn sheet, pencil a cross 3 cm right of the new sheet's middle and prick it once with the compass point; check the compass still spans 40 mm on a ruler (re-set it if not) and its pencil is sharp; stand it with the point in the prick and the pencil 4 cm forward of it. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The pad is a rigid 6 mm block (a 50-sheet pad does not bend here); the prick is a 1.0 mm square hole 1.5 mm deep. The compass is boxes, cylinders and capsules (no knurling); its hinge is a joint with 0.10 N m Coulomb friction (an estimate for a tightened hinge). No graphite is laid down: the scorer tracks where the pencil's point touched, and visual-only marks (1.2 mm wide) show the line; a breaking point is a 5 N limit (estimate). Frictions are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.004 (the right gripper hovered by the pad's near right corner and never took the handle; near step 1,600 the compass toppled over onto the pad, its pencil drawing about 2 deg as it fell); demo: 1.0
